about.title: Huron Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Huron is a small farming community in Fresno County, and many residents travel outside town for hospital care or rely on limited local clinics for treatment. When that care falls below the accepted standard, the effects can be serious and lasting, whether the error happened at a nearby hospital, an urgent care visit, or a follow-up appointment. Medical malpractice cases are different from most injury claims — California's MICRA law sets strict timelines and requires input from a qualified medical expert before a case can move forward. We review medical records, evaluate whether the standard of care was met, and explain your options plainly. If you or a family member in Huron were harmed by a delayed diagnosis, medication mistake, or surgical error, getting an early review matters because some deadlines are shorter than people expect.

whyChoose.title: Why Timing and Expert Review Matter in Huron

items.title: Short, Strict Deadlines
items.desc: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from when you discovered the harm and no more than three years from the date of the injury to act. A 90-day pre-suit notice is also required before a lawsuit can be filed, so waiting can cost you options.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California law nearly always requires a qualified medical expert to confirm that the care fell below an accepted standard. A poor outcome by itself does not mean malpractice occurred, so this step is central to any claim.

items.title: Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises Yearly
items.desc: MICRA places a statutory limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, though that cap increases each year. Our team familiar with the current figures can explain how it may apply to your situation.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires proof that the care provided fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. That's why an early expert review is such an important part of any claim.

items.question: Where would my case be handled if I live in Huron?
items.answer: Because Huron sits within Fresno County, claims connected to care received here or at nearby facilities are typically pursued through the Fresno County court system. We can confirm the right venue based on where the treatment occurred.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered the injury, and no more than three years from when it happened, though a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement can affect your timeline. Because these rules are strict and fact-specific, it helps to have your situation reviewed sooner rather than later.
